feedback: Reject and repair the SHACL logic. The exact Table 8 SPARQL constraint has accidental pass logic: its FILTER selects rows where the required grade is correct, so compliant cases are reported as violations while incorrect or missing selections can pass. Invert the condition so the constraint selects a case when no exact table selection matches, while preserving NOT_APPLICABLE behavior. Both applicability and exact-selection queries also bind ?ship as any ship having polarClass, without connecting it to the focus case; bind the supplied owner path (`?ship nltl:hasSteelGradeRequirementCase $this`) before using that ship's polarClass, so a different ship cannot satisfy the case. Retain the existing case-owned selectors, Table 8 reference, exact required-grade result, and same-strength-family rank comparison.

Reject and repair the semantic logic. Although the case-to-ship binding and inverted NOT EXISTS direction now address the prior defects, the applicability FILTER only covers material class three, normal-strength steel, thickness 35–50 mm, and selected Polar Classes. It omits all applicable Table 8 rows for thickness bands below 35 mm, high-tensile steel, material classes one/two, and other Polar Class groups, allowing missing required grades to pass. The required-grade alternatives also do not faithfully reproduce the supplied table: for example, material class two selections for 10–35 mm are missing, and the 35–50 mm class-three normal-strength branches and Polar Class limits are incomplete or incorrect. Replace the hard-coded applicability and grade predicates with complete, mutually exclusive Table 8 selection coverage using all supplied thickness bands, material classes, strength categories, Polar Class groups, and NOT_APPLICABLE rows. Also enforce that actual and required grades belong to the same strength-category family; the current actual-grade sh:in permits cross-family values and the rank query skips mismatched families, causing an accidental pass. Preserve the case-owned selectors, Table 8 reference, exact required-grade result, and same-family rank comparison.
